reference: Слово 1, заглавие (Догматико-полемические сочинения, гл. 6; «Два слова против Магомета», 1910): «скверного пса Магомета»; Слово 2, заглавие: «пса Магомета»
gist_en: The titles call Muhammad a 'vile dog' and a 'dog'. It is a personal insult in the title, not a doctrinal argument.
why_excluded: Personal insult (exclusion rule 3). Titles only, not quoted as passages; the works are still listed in works.json with the insult flagged.

reference: Слово 1 (гл. 6), раздел о рассказе о Магомете и жене (paragraph after the 'Jewish teacher' legend): «нечестивого народа аравийского, занятого скотоводством и живущего по-скотски»; «скотоподобных тех варваров»
gist_en: Maxim describes the Arab people as godless, cattle-herding and living like beasts, and calls the people 'beast-like barbarians'.
why_excluded: Ethnic insult against a people (exclusion rule 3). Not quoted. The Jewish and Arian legend in the earlier part of the work is kept as maxim_p02 and is not affected.

reference: Ответы христиан против агарян (гл. 8, paraklit.org): «богомерзких агарян»; «бесовдохновенная их книга» (the epithet is kept in maxim_p05)
gist_en: Maxim calls Muslims 'abominable Hagarenes' and their book demon-inspired.
why_excluded: Insult against a people (the 'abominable' epithet); the book epithet is kept only inside maxim_p05 where the doctrinal point is the Qur'an's praise of the Gospel. Orchestrator may cut it.

reference: Нестор-Искандер, Повесть о взятии Царьграда турками в 1453 году (ИРЛИ, Библиотека литературы Древней Руси, т. 7; read at lib.pushkinskijdom.ru): epithets «безбожный Магомет», «безвѣрный Магмет» for Mehmed II in the siege narrative
gist_en: The siege narrative calls Mehmed II the 'godless Mahomet' and 'faithless Mahmet', with personal insults; no doctrine.
why_excluded: Personal insults against a ruler (Mehmed II, not Muhammad), inside a military narrative; no doctrinal statement about Islam found in the text read (rule 3). Not quoted.
